title: Crossplane comm failure modes and microburst characterization
content:
Purpose:
Summarize a set of experiments that reproduced a specific multi‑GPU communication failure / tail‑latency event we saw in production: short-lived NVLink/NCCL microbursts that cause host queue stalls and unexpected retries in our RPC path. Goal is to document failure modes, narrow root causes, and capture low‑risk mitigations to validate in staging before any global rollout.

Executive summary (top lines):
- Observed tail-latency spikes at P99.9 for gpt-13B-ish models when running tensor+pipeline parallel configurations across mixed NVLink islands.
- Root trigger: short (~200–800us) sustained link congestion events during KV-cache warmup + attention recompute, causing host-side queue stalls and NCCL-level packet retransmit/backoff in some firmwares.
- Amplified by: heterogeneous interconnect topologies (islanded NVLink), small interleaved batches (seq=2048, batch=1–4), and aggressive NCCL rendezvous timeouts configured in our runtime.
- Low-effort mitigations with immediate positive impact: pacing injection at host transfer layer, increase NCCL socket buffer sizing, and short randomized jitter on batch arrival to avoid synchronized bursts.

Experimental setup (hardware + software):
- Cluster: 8× A100-80GB per node, two nodes connected via NVLink bridge + RoCEv2 network between nodes. Tests repeated on a 4×A100 node (single node islanded NVLink topology) and a heterogeneous mix (A100 + A10m) to stress driver fallback.
- OS/kernel: Ubuntu 22.04, NVIDIA driver 535.54, CUDA 12.1, NCCL 2.18.3.
- Runtime: redwood-serving v1.14.2 (experimental comm scheduler enabled), custom patch to log NCCL transport events (see PR).
- Model: gpt-style causal model, 13B params, sharded with tensor-parallel (TP=2) + pipeline-parallel (PP=2) across 4 GPUs for the main test.
- Workload: steady stream of inference requests with sequence lengths 512/1024/2048 mixed, dynamic batching enabled with max_batch=8, beta traffic generator with replay of production traces.

Reproduction recipe (short):
1) Deploy runtime with experimental comm-scheduler env var: REDWOOD_COMM_SCHED=1 and NCCL_SOCKET_NTHREADS=4.
2) Start 2 nodes with node0: GPUs 0–3 local NVLink island, node1: GPUs 4–7. Use our trace replayer at 400 rps (seq distribution [512:60%,1024:30%,2048:10%]).
3) Monitor: nvlink stats (/sys/class/net/...), nvidia-smi dmon, and custom nccl-telemetry logs at info level.
4) Expect to see P99.9 spikes after ~12–20 minutes as KV-cache warming synchronizes.

Key observations (detailed):
- Timing of bursts: recurring microburst windows observed roughly every 40–60s during the first 5 minutes of a session; correlated with large KV-cache writeback and slice-based recompute (attention layer recompute triggered by memory pressure).
- Packet behavior: NCCL logs show repeated "send retry" events with ~3–9 retries and an exponential backoff that aligns with observed latency spikes.
- Host queue occupancy: when spikes occur, host-to-device PCIe queues and RoCE send queues reach transient saturation and the runtime enqueue latency jumps from ~120us -> 3–12ms for some requests.
- Asymmetry: downstream GPUs on the same NVLink island often finish earlier, but cross-node rendezvous hangs until the slowest link resumes, increasing end-to-end tail by >8×.
- Firmware sensitivity: when repeating tests on driver 535.80 (newer), microbursts were less frequent but still present; suggests partial mitigation in NIC/driver but not eliminated.

Representative logs (stripped):
[2025-08-20 13:22:07.941] nccl: send retry (chan 1) attempts=4 wait=320us
[2025-08-20 13:22:07.942] runtime: host-queue-latency sample=11.2ms ctx=kv_writeback
[2025-08-20 13:22:08.003] kernel: roce send queue full, enqueued=0 drop=0

Small experiment table (high level):
- Baseline (no pacing): P99=32ms, P99.9=198ms, throughput=380rps steady
- Add host pacing (inject 150–300us spacing between host transfers): P99=26ms, P99.9=65ms, throughput=360rps
- Increase NCCL socket buf (NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 + net.core.rmem_default=524288): P99.9 improved to 72ms, less frequent retries
- Small randomized inter-request jitter (0–200us): reduced synchronization spikes, median unchanged, P99.9 ~70ms

Hypotheses and root cause threads considered:
- Microburst origin: KV-cache warmup leads to synchronous large host transfers from multiple ranks; these coalesce on the interconnect causing transient link saturation.
- NCCL behavior: rendezvous algorithm is sensitive to packet loss/retry; default backoff penalties compound host-level enqueuing that blocks the runtime.
- Firmware/driver: NIC firmware can coalesce or smooth some bursts, but not all; driver-level queue management interacts with our scheduling inside the runtime.

Low-risk mitigations (recommended order for staging validation):
1) Host-side pacing shim: add a 100–300us spacing window between large host-to-device transfers across ranks during KV-cache writeback. Quick A/B tests show large tail improvements.
2) Small randomized jitter on request arrival at the orchestration layer to avoid simultaneous KV-cache warmups across ranks.
3) Increase NCCL and kernel socket buffers when running across RoCE backplanes. Documented cpu sysctl and NCCL envs included below.
4) Investigate using NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL (where supported) to prefer NVLink for intra-node where possible; requires topology-aware rank placement.

Riskier / longer-term actions:
- Implement a comm-scheduler that can observe upcoming large transfers and serialize them across ranks (requires more runtime instrumentation).
- Collaborate with NIC vendor for improved hardware pacing or firmware that supports microburst shaping.
- Evaluate moving KV-cache population off the critical path (background population with higher priority prefetching).

Runtime knobs we tested (useful command snippets):
- sysctl -w net.core.rmem_default=524288
- sysctl -w net.core.wmem_default=524288
- export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0; export NCCL_SOCKET_NTHREADS=4; export NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL
- REDWOOD_COMM_PACING_US=200 (experimental env we added)

Open questions / next steps:
- Should pace only KV-cache phases or all host transfers? Tradeoff: selective pacing keeps throughput higher but needs accurate detection.
- How does this interact with our autoscaler which may burst-shift traffic during scale events?
- Need a canonical test harness for microburst reproduction that CI can run nightly.
- Validate on other hardware (H100, older A100 driver combos) and on private-deploy setups (VPC with different RoCE offloads).

Attachments / where to look for raw artifacts:
- nccl-telemetry captures (s3://redwood-debug/crossplane/2025-08-20.tar.gz)
- perf counters summary (pdf) attached to Jira JIRA-RT-912
- PR with logging and REDWOOD_COMM_PACING implementation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/478

Action items (owners):
- Asha: wire up host pacing as an opt-in runtime flag and run two overnight stagers (due 2025-08-22).
- Diego: run firmware/driver matrix on H100 + A100 combos, capture nccl telemetry (due 2025-08-28).
- Sana: add microburst scenario to performance harness and open a CI job draft (due 2025-09-04).
- Jon: draft a short runbook for on-call to identify these microburst events and toggle REDWOOD_COMM_PACING in staging (due 2025-08-25).

Notes to self / raw thoughts:
- We should be careful not to conflate P99.9 regressions from model compute variance vs comm microbursts — add synthetic compute-only baseline.
- Some earlier tests showed benefit when we moved to circ-buffered host transfers (copy into big pinned buffer and stream) — worth trying combined with pacing.
- Keep an eye on cost: too much pacing reduces throughput; try adaptive pacing guided by queue depth signals instead of fixed us.

References and background reading:
- NCCL internals notes (internal wiki): confluence:NCCl-internals
- Prior microburst memos: team/member notes from 2024 labeled "microburst-mitigation" (search drive)

End of note.
